title: Take a plugged cord out of a board hole and bin it
instruction: Take the grey cord out of the hole in the wooden board, drop it into the blue bin and let go of it.
context: Recycling and reclamation workers (O*NET 53-7062.04) "sort materials ... into appropriate containers for recycling", and the EU WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU, Annex VII) lists external electric cables among components to be removed from separately collected e-waste. Toy-scale mock-up: a cord threaded through a hole with a moulded plug must come out towards the plug side, since pulling the bare end jams the plug. Intended solution: one arm withdraws it and hands it over the board to the other.
setup: Station table; cm from the point midway between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Board: dark-brown stained plywood (or brown PLA) 24 x 1.2 x 5 cm, upright on the midline (faces at y -0.6 and +0.6), x 18-42, screwed down; 14 x 14 mm square hole at x 29.3-30.7, 8-22 mm above the table. Cord: grey 6 mm round PVC cord, 30 cm, lying straight along y at x 30 through the hole. Bare end on the right-arm side at y -12, finished with a copper 10 x 8 x 8 mm crimp (fits through the hole). Other end at y +18, moulded into a black plug 40 x 24 x 18 mm (long side along the cord, 18 g), centre x 30, y 20. Bin: blue PLA open box, inside 18 x 16 cm (x 24-42, y -32 to -16), 5 mm walls, 4 cm tall, screwed down. Board and bin are fixed; nothing else on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end (tape measure / photo). Score 0 if the cord still passes through the hole, or a gripper is still holding the cord, plug or crimp (gripper centre within 3 cm of any of them). Otherwise 0.3 + 0.7 x (fraction of the cord's length, crimp to plug tip, lying inside the bin's inner walls and below its rim); 1.0 when the whole cord, plug and crimp lie in the bin (success, must hold 1 s).
reset_notes: Thread the crimp end back through the hole from the plug side and lay the cord straight along the x 30 tape line: crimp centre at y -12.5 on the right-arm side, plug flat (long side along the cord) with its centre at y 20 on the left-arm side. Check the bin is empty and board and bin are still screwed down.
fidelity: Cord: 15 rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no stretch, no twist, no plasticity; plug and crimp are rigid boxes welded to the ends. Board and bin are rigid and fixed; the hole is square (4 mm clearance round the cord). The plug cannot pass the hole in sim (rigid colliders); in the real kit it is far larger than the hole and cannot pass without breaking the board. The sim cannot tear the cord or break the board, so damage is not scored.
